title: Hazardous Area Classification
short: Identifying where explosive gas or dust atmospheres can occur, and defining the zones that govern equipment selection.
metaDescription: Hazardous area classification for industrial sites in South Africa: identifying explosive gas and dust atmospheres, defining zones and documenting the basis for Ex equipment selection.
lead: Every decision about electrical equipment in a hazardous location starts with a sound classification. We assess where flammable gases, vapours or combustible dusts may be present, how often, and for how long — and document the result so that the right equipment is specified and installed.
body: A hazardous area is defined by three main criteria: the type of hazard (the gas or dust group), the auto-ignition temperature of the hazardous material (the temperature or “T” rating), and the likelihood of the hazard being present in flammable concentrations (the zone).

Getting these criteria right determines which protection concepts and equipment categories are acceptable in each part of a plant. An overly conservative classification adds cost; an under-classified area creates real ignition risk. Our role is to help you reach a classification that is defensible, practical and clearly documented.
points: Identification of sources of release for flammable gases, vapours and combustible dusts
Zone definition for gas (Zones 0, 1, 2) and dust (Zones 20, 21, 22) atmospheres
Gas / dust group and temperature class (T-rating) determination
Documentation to support Ex equipment selection, installation and inspection
audience: New installations, plant changes and extensions

title: Electrical & Earthing Audits
short: Independent inspection of electrical installations and earthing systems, with clear findings you can act on.
metaDescription: Electrical and earthing audits by Brain Industries: inspection of electrical installations and earthing systems with clear, prioritised findings for plant and maintenance teams.
lead: Installations change over time — equipment is added, modified and exposed to harsh conditions. A structured audit establishes the actual condition of your electrical installation and earthing system, and gives your team a prioritised list of what needs attention.
body: An electrical inspection, or periodic inspection, helps prevent future mishaps caused by issues within your electrical system, including malfunctions and fires. Earthing and bonding deserve particular attention: they protect people against electric shock, allow protective devices to operate correctly and, in hazardous areas, help prevent incendive sparks and static build-up.
Our audits are practical. Findings are recorded clearly so that maintenance, operations and management can see what was inspected, what was found and what corrective action is recommended.
points: Visual and physical inspection of electrical installations and equipment
Inspection of earthing and bonding arrangements
Electrical audits in hazardous (Ex) areas
Clear, prioritised findings and recommended corrective actions

title: Electrical & Hazardous Area Installations
short: Electrical installation work for general industrial and hazardous (Ex) environments, from panels to field equipment.
metaDescription: Electrical and hazardous area (Ex) installations by Brain Industries, Pretoria: control stations, panels, distribution boards and field equipment for industrial environments.
lead: Hazardous area installations have to be right first time. Equipment must suit the classified zone, gas or dust group and temperature class, and it must be installed so that its protection concept is maintained. We carry out electrical installation work for both general industrial and Ex environments.
body: Our installation work covers the equipment that keeps a plant running — local control stations, panels, distribution boards and the associated cabling and field equipment. In hazardous areas, the integrity of each installation depends on details such as correct cable entry, gland selection, sealing and earthing.
Where required, installations can be followed by inspection and documentation, so that you have a clear record of what was installed and its condition at handover.
points: Local control stations, panels and distribution boards
Installation of explosion-protected (Ex) equipment
Cabling, cable entries and glanding appropriate to the protection concept
Earthing and bonding of installed equipment

title: Electrical Certificate of Compliance
short: Inspection and testing of electrical installations for the issuing of a Certificate of Compliance (CoC).
metaDescription: Electrical Certificates of Compliance (CoC) in Pretoria and Gauteng: inspection and testing of electrical installations in line with the Electrical Installation Regulations.
lead: A Certificate of Compliance (CoC) confirms that an electrical installation has been inspected and tested and meets the applicable requirements. It is required under the Electrical Installation Regulations, issued in terms of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 85 of 1993.
body: A CoC is typically required for new installations, alterations and additions, and when a property changes ownership. It must be issued by a registered person after the installation has been inspected and tested.
We inspect and test the installation, identify anything that needs to be corrected and, once the installation complies, issue the certificate and supporting test report.
points: Inspection and testing of electrical installations
Identification of non-compliances and required remedial work
Certificate of Compliance and test report
Supplementary certificates for alterations and additions

title: Auto Bindicators
short: Rotary paddle level indicators for bins, silos and hoppers holding bulk solids.
metaDescription: Auto bindicators (rotary paddle level indicators) for bins, silos and hoppers containing bulk materials, supplied by Brain Industries.
lead: A bindicator is a rotary paddle level indicator. A slowly rotating paddle is mounted through the wall of a bin, silo or hopper; when bulk material reaches the paddle and stops it turning, the unit switches a signal — indicating high, low or intermediate level.
body: Level indication helps prevent overfilling, running empty and the downtime and spillage that come with both. Bindicators are a simple, robust way of providing that signal for bulk solids such as grain, powders, aggregates and similar materials.
Contact us with your application — the material, vessel and installation conditions — and we will advise on a suitable unit.
points: Rotary paddle level indication for bulk solids
High, low and intermediate level detection
For bins, silos, hoppers and chutes
Application advice on selection and installation

title: Safety Roto Reflectors

metaDescription: Safety Roto Reflectors from Brain Industries: rotating reflectors in a range of colours for improved visibility of equipment, vehicles and obstacles.
lead: Safety Roto Reflectors are rotating reflectors. As the unit turns, its reflective cups catch and return light from changing angles — creating movement that draws the eye far more effectively than a static reflector.
body: They are available in a range of colours, which allows colour coding of equipment, routes or hazards.
Please contact us for mounting options, colours and quantities.

title: LED Lighting
short: LED lighting for industrial applications, including the HALO range.
metaDescription: LED lighting for industrial applications, including the HALO range, supplied by Brain Industries South Africa.
lead: Good lighting is a safety requirement, not a luxury. We supply LED lighting for industrial applications, including the HALO range, and can advise on fittings for general and hazardous area use.
body: LED lighting reduces energy consumption and maintenance compared with older lamp technologies, which matters where fittings are difficult or costly to access.

In hazardous areas, light fittings must be certified for the zone, group and temperature class in which they are installed. We can help you select lighting that suits both the task and the classification.
